title: fix(linux): recover completed Quick Chat replies without resending
body:
Related: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/145355

Stack 4/8, replayed onto main after the preceding layer landed.
Previous: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/146047 | Next: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/146049

This same-repository branch is writable by maintainers with push access.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes Quick Chat remaining busy after a completed turn loses its acknowledgement, or sending a queued draft to a replacement Gateway.

## User Impact

Retrying an unchanged draft can recover the completed reply without generating a second provider turn. Incomplete or unrelated history remains an error.

## Why This Change Was Made

Carry the selected Gateway generation through socket dispatch, preserve the original retry key, and recover only its bounded, matching terminal history. The replay preserves current desktop request and sleep ownership checks, including a selected configuration at the actual socket enqueue.

The existing Canvas refresh and widget command interfaces remain unchanged until the next stack layer.

## Evidence

- Current replay: 22 renderer tests passed, with targeted TypeScript lint/format and JavaScript syntax checks. The desktop cleared-route wire control checks configuration absence independently of matching generation IDs.
- Reused aggregate native proof: an isolated real Gateway and deterministic provider recovered a lost-ACK turn with the same key and no second provider turn. This is historical behavior proof, not a native run of this replay.
- Scoped composition review completed; its cross-platform test-constructor correction is included. The other reported platform issue was excluded by the existing Linux-only match-arm guard.
- Current replay native proof: Rust 1.98.1 formatting/build passed; gateway dispatch tests passed 38 with one X11-only test intentionally ignored, desktop owner tests passed 2, and sleep tests passed 17 including six private-logind cases. [Native run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/34771579815). The ignored test is not counted as a pass; this is Linux proof, not cross-compilation.
- [LinuxApp at the tested replay](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/34772334949) passed formatting, Rust tests/build, the inline-browser flow and mac companion checks. Packaging and first-run steps were skipped.
- Current signed head `4389b0d3218f7a4c9a957bf4b08f0c03b6d7cfbe` syncs main to inherit the unrelated Workboard lint repair in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/147203. Its complete four-path delta is byte-identical to tested replay `c59470f2c184271db69898faec68ac7329c0098b`; no Linux behavior was changed for that CI failure. [Fresh-head LinuxApp](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/34773059674) passed Linux formatting, Rust tests/build, inline-browser and mac companion checks; packaging and first-run remained skipped. [Fresh-head core CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/34773059675) and its required gate passed.

Native behavior evidence used the recorded X11/Xvfb functional graphics profile. Default graphics, Wayland, packaged installation and performance are not qualified by this PR.
